prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Now spring appears, with beauty crowned And all is light and life around, Why comes not Jane? When friendship calls, Why leaves she not Augusta’s walls? Where cooling zephyrs faintly blow, Nor spread the cheering, healthful glow That glides through each awakened vein, As skimming o’er the spacious plain, We look around with joyous eye, And view no boundaries but the sky. Already April’s reign is o’er, Her evening tints delight no more; No more the violet scents the gale, No more the mist o’erspreads the vale; The lovely queen of smiles and tears, Who gave thee birth, no more appears; But blushing May, with brow serene, And vestments of a livelier green, Commands the winged choir to sing, And with wild notes the meadows ring. O come! ere all the train is gone, No more to hail thy twenty-one; That age which higher honour shares, And well become the wreath it wears. From lassitude and cities flee, And breathe the air of heaven, with me.

outputs.L1:
Here are two options for polishing the text, depending on the format you prefer:

### Option 1: Sophisticated Formal Prose
*Best if you want to turn the verse into an elegant, highly polished written invitation or letter.*

> Spring has arrived in all its radiant glory, awakening the countryside with light and vitality. Yet, as friendship warmly calls, why do you linger within Augusta’s walls? The faint breezes of the city offer none of the invigorating warmth that stirs the spirit when roaming across the open plains, where the eye beholds no boundary but the endless sky. 
> 
> April—that season of smiles and tears in which you were born—has drawn to a close. Her soft evening hues, the fragrance of violets on the wind, and the valley mists have all faded away. In her place, May has arrived with serene grace and vibrant greenery, summoning the birds to fill the meadows with joyful song. 
> 
> Please join me before these glorious days slip away, so that we may celebrate your twenty-first birthday—a remarkable milestone that deserves to be honored in full. Escape the weariness of the city, and come breathe the pure, reviving air of the open countryside with me.

---

### Option 2: Refined Poetic Verse
*Best if you wish to preserve the original rhyming poetic structure while improving its rhythm, flow, and grandeur.*

> Now spring arrives, with radiant beauty crowned,  
> And light and life now flourish all around.  
> Why lingers Jane? When friendship warmly calls,  
> Why leaves she not Augusta’s city walls?  
> Where feeble breezes faintly, weakly blow,  
> Bereft of that vibrant, invigorating glow  
> That surges through each reawakened vein,  
> As, sweeping o'er the wide, unbounded plain,  
> We gaze around us with a joyful eye,  
> Beholding no horizon save the sky.  
> 
> April’s gentle reign is now no more;  
> Her evening hues delight the sights no more.  
> No longer violets scent the passing gale,  
> Nor morning mists enshroud the quiet vale.  
> That lovely queen of sudden smiles and tears—  
> Who blessed your birth—no longer now appears.  
> But blushing May, with countenance serene  
> And robes adorned in vibrant, living green,  
> Commands the winged chorus now to sing,  
> Till wild and sweet the sunny meadows ring.  
> 
> O come! Before this fleeting train is gone,  
> To celebrate your milestone twenty-one—  
> An age that higher honor justly shares,  
> Well suited to the noble wreath it wears.  
> From city life and weariness now flee,  
> And breathe the pure, fresh air of heaven with me.

***

**Key Information Retained in Both Versions:**
* The arrival of spring and the call of friendship.
* The request for Jane to leave Augusta (the city).
* The contrast between stagnant city air and invigorating country air with wide horizons.
* The transition from April (Jane's birth month) to May.
* The birds singing in the green meadows.
* The celebration of Jane's 21st birthday.
* The invitation to escape city fatigue and enjoy nature together.

Despite her friend's eager summons, she remains behind the city walls of Augusta. The weak breezes there fail to offer the invigorating, health-restoring energy that surges through a person's veins out in the open country, where one can gaze happily across expansive fields with no horizon but the sky.

April has already drawn to a close, taking with it the beauty of its twilight hues, the perfume of violets carried on the wind, and the fog resting over the valleys. That month of alternating rain and sunshine, which brought Jane into the world, has officially passed. In its place, a calm May has arrived, clothed in vibrant green foliage and prompting the birds to fill the pastures with their wild songs.

Jane must hurry to visit before this seasonal procession slips away, so they can honor her twenty-first milestone—an age of elevated prestige that truly deserves to be celebrated. She needs to escape urban weariness and join the speaker to inhale the pure, divine air of the countryside.
outputs.L3:
Dearest Jane,

Spring has finally arrived, bathing the world in a brilliant, gentle light and a beauty that feels entirely new. As I look around at this radiant morning, I cannot help but wonder why you still linger behind the dull, heavy walls of the city. What keeps you captive there when your friend is eagerly waiting to welcome you here?

Out in the open countryside, the atmosphere is utterly refreshing and health-giving—a place where the spirit naturally lightens and finds pure joy beneath wide, expansive skies. The quiet days of April have now given way to the warmth of May, dressing the hills in richer, livelier shades of green while the trees resound with the cheerful, tireless singing of birds. 

It seems only right that you should celebrate your momentous twenty-first birthday during such a vibrant season. Marking this landmark step into adulthood surrounded by the blooming vitality of nature is a joy you truly deserve.

I earnestly urge you to flee the noise and weariness of city life, if only for a short while. Come away to the fields, breathe the crisp, sweet air of the countryside, and embrace the beauty of this place before the glory of the season slips away. 

With fondest love,

Your Friend
outputs.L4:
To Jane, on the Eve of Her Twenty-First Year:

The meadows have fully awakened, Jane, yet the sweetest bloom of the season remains tragically absent. Out here, beyond the reach of iron gates and paved avenues, May has unfolded her full, radiant majesty. The rolling hills are cloaked in a fresh emerald mantle, the wild clover perfumes the morning breeze, and the river hums an unending song of rebirth. Every tree glistens with new life, and the open sky stretches out, vast and unobstructed. Yet, for all this vibrant splendor, there is a quiet vacancy in the countryside—a hollow space that only your presence can fill.

Why do you linger in Augusta? How can you endure the suffocating air of the city, where the dust settles heavy on the spirits and the horizon is imprisoned by towering spires of brick and stone? The city demands your restraint, binding your wild grace to crowded avenues and stifling parlors. It dulls the brightness of the season, exchanging the perfume of blossoms for soot and steam, and replacing the melody of nature with the restless, artificial clamor of urban life. Augusta is a place of walls; you were made for horizons.

I poetically entreat you: leave it all behind. Cast off the grey monotony of the city and fly to the open fields, where your spirit may finally breathe again. Fleeing the urban cage will allow nature to work its quiet magic upon you, washing away the fatigue of the town and revitalizing your weary soul. Feel the unbridled wind untangle your hair, tread barefoot upon the cool moss, and drink in the untamed freedom that only the wilderness can offer. Out here, freedom is not merely a concept—it is the very air we draw into our lungs.

Consider, too, the sacred timing of this hour. You stand today upon the golden threshold of your twenty-first year—a momentous milestone that marks the true flowering of your youth. Such an occasion ought not to be wasted amidst the dim lamps and closed curtains of Augusta. A milestone so grand demands a celebration crafted by Earth itself. No month but May, in all its fertile, blossoming glory, is fit to mirror the bright future that lies before you. 

Come, Jane. Leave the suffocating city to its dust and embrace the wild freedom that calls your name. Let the woodland birds sing your birthday anthem, let the wild grass carpet your path, and celebrate your twenty-first year beneath an unbounded canopy of stars. The countryside is waiting, breathless and bright, to welcome you home to nature—and home to yourself.
outputs.L5:
We spend much of our lives waiting for the right moment, often forgetting that the only terrain we truly inhabit is **Now**. The past is an echo, and the future is merely a possibility, but *Now* is where life actually happens. It is the precise second where breath meets lungs, where choices are forged, and where potential transforms into reality. To be present *Now* is to accept the immediate truth of our existence.

Yet, no moment stands in complete isolation. Life is not a series of disconnected flashes, but a continuous stream. That continuity is sustained by a simple, quiet bridge: **And**. This small word is the ultimate promise of momentum. We experience hardship, *And* we heal. We reach a milestone, *And* we keep walking. "And" connects our solitary present to the vast tapestry of what comes next, reminding us that no single chapter is the whole story.

Standing in the present, moving toward the future, we inevitably face the deepest impulse of the human spirit: **Why**. "Why" is the engine of inquiry and the compass of purpose. It is not enough simply to exist in the *Now*, nor is it enough to endlessly add another "And" to our days. We need to know the reason behind the rhythm. "Why" challenges us to seek meaning, to question our path, and to align our actions with something greater than mere survival.

Together, these three words form the architecture of a conscious life:

**Why** gives us our purpose. 
**Now** gives us our starting point. 
**And** gives us the courage to continue.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an 18th-century style poem in rhyming iambic tetrameter couplets where the speaker invites a friend named Jane to leave the city and join them in the countryside to celebrate her 21st birthday in May.
counterfactuals.output:
Forsake, fair Jane, the smoky town,
And lay thy heavy burdens down;
Abandon now the noisy throngs,
For gentle shades and woodland songs.

For lo! the merry month of May
Adorns the earth in bright array,
And marks the day that gave thee birth
With gentle ease and harmless mirth.

Full twenty-one bright years have flown
Since first thy youthful beauty shone;
Thy vernal prime is now complete,
Where innocence and virtue meet.

The verdant meads invite thy tread,
Where roses blush and lilies spread;
The silver brooks sweet music yield,
And blossoms sweeten every field.

No dusty streets, no city din,
Shall interrupt the peace within;
In nature's bower we shall twine
A floral crown for brow of thine.

Then haste, sweet Jane, and come away,
To greet the sun and hail the day;
Leave care behind, and come to see
How rustic shades do welcome thee!
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.output:
The city wears a cloak of gray,
Where heavy walls shut out the day;
The iron wheels and crowded street
Afflict the mind and tire the feet.

But here, sweet Jane, the meadows bloom,
And zephyrs chase away the gloom;
The winter cold at last has fled,
And verdant moss makes soft our bed.

Now nature wakes the sleeping earth
To crown the morning of your birth;
Full twenty-one swift years have run
To meet you in this golden sun.

The shepherd tunes his oaten reed,
The cattle graze upon the mead,
And crystal waters softly flow
Where early buds of clover grow.

We’ll weave a wreath of primrose pale,
And violets gathered in the vale,
To deck your brow and hail the year
With gentle mirth and rural cheer.

So leave the walls of smoke and stone,
And make these quiet hills your own;
Come fly the town, sweet Jane, and bring
Your twenty-first delightful spring!

counterfactuals.output:
Now April sheds her last, reluctant shower,
And yields the landscape to a warmer hour;
Fair May advances, crowned with buds and dew,
To deck the countryside in green anew.
Bright Phoebus drives his golden car on high,
And clears the cloudy shadows from the sky,
While Zephyr whispers through the blooming bower,
To wake the fragrance of the vernal flower.

On this blest morn, a bright design appears,
To mark the summit of thy twenty years;
Full twenty-one fair springs have softly flown,
And virtue claims thee, lovely, for her own.
Yet why, sweet Jane, in brick-bound walls reside,
Where towering spires the vault of heaven hide?
Where noisy streets and murky vapors rise,
And obscure the splendor of the open skies?

When all the riches of the May are thine?
Leave the dull city, where the spirit pines,
To seek the shelter of the country vines;
Come, drink the ether of the western gale,
Where health and freedom bloom in every vale.

Haste, gentle friend, forsake the crowded town,
And wear the meadow’s freshly woven crown;
Let rolling fields thy happy footsteps greet,

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a poem in the style of Phillis Wheatley or Hannah More addressed to a girl named Jane on her 21st birthday, contrasting the stagnant air of the town with the blooming beauty of May.
counterfactuals.output:
**To Miss Jane, on the Completion of Her Twenty-First Year**

Hail, gentle Jane! now stepped on womanhood’s stage,
And doubly blessed in this thy blooming age;
Twice ten and one bright suns have rolled away,
To crown thy virtues in the month of May.

Far from the town, where sluggish vapors rise,
And murky mists obscure the azure skies;
Where stagnant air in heavy languor creeps,
And artful pride its restless vigil keeps—
There prisoned souls in dull confinement mourn,
By empty noise and gilded follies torn;
No fragrant breeze the fainting spirit cheers,
Where worldly tumult duds the passing years.

How blest the change where vernal breezes blow,
And opening blossoms in effulgence glow!
Where gentle Zephyr sweeps the verdant plain,
And nature breaks her wintry, iron chain.
From every bough the feathered choir prolongs
Their grateful hymns and soft, untutored songs;
Creation smiles, by Providence arrayed,
In purest green and floral grace displayed.

So let thy mind, fair Jane, untainted bloom,
Above the city’s mist and sullen gloom.
While fainting crowds in heavy streets delay,
May thy pure breast reflect the breath of May!
Though earthly youth must fade as seasons fly,
A virtuous soul shall bloom eternally:
Let Wisdom guide thy footsteps as they rise,
And lift thy hopes to mansions in the skies.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
